transcript.text: Bosch PIE631BB5E hob switched one zone off and shows F2 while I was batch cooking on all four rings. What does F2 mean?

I have noted the F2 code on your Bosch display; while this is just a controller report and not proof of a failed part, this step is the right place to start regardless. The type of hob you have changes what we need to check next. Is it an induction hob (only works with magnetic pans), a ceramic hob (smooth glass that glows red), a solid-plate hob, or gas?
It's an induction hob - a Bosch PIE631BB5E, about a year old. The F2 only came up during the long batch cooking session.

Thanks for letting us know about the induction issue. Please remember that induction cooking only works with magnetic pans, so you should check if a fridge magnet sticks firmly to the base of your cookware. Try using a pan that you know works on the other zones and place it centred on this specific zone. Does a known-good pan heat on this zone, or does it fail too?

The pans are fine, they work normally on every zone, including this one. It only cuts out during long heavy use like the batch cooking, and the fan was running loudly when it happened. Does that help explain the F2?

[Heading: Pan not suiting induction]
Thanks for checking that with another pan. Since the hob works fine with a suitable pan, the issue lies with the cookware rather than the appliance itself. Induction hobs require pans with a flat, magnetic base large enough to cover the heating zone. You can verify this by ensuring a fridge magnet sticks firmly to the bottom of your pan. As the hob is functioning correctly, no repair or replacement parts are needed for this unit.
